newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CAPE FRUIT CROP HIT BY LENGTHY S.AFRICAN WINTER.
newsitem.headline: CAPE FRUIT CROP HIT BY LENGTHY S.AFRICAN WINTER.

text.p: A late rainy winter season had affected the volumes of fruit produced in the Western Cape for the export market, fruit exporter Unifruco said on Thursday.
Andrew Southwood, Unifruco market development manager, said apricot, nectarine and peach volumes had been affected but it was still too early to quantify the extent to which targets would not be met.
The Cape's usual rainy winter lasted well into November this year with a few cold spells also seen in December.
"But the fruit that has been sent out has been of good quality and the market has received it well," Southwood said.

"It has been an unusual season. Last year we had similar problems at the beginning of the season but it seemed to clear up earlier whereas this season the colder weather seemed to persist far longer," he said.

For the third year in a row, Unifruco had chartered Boeing 747s and Antanov 124s from South African Airways and British charter companies to airlift Thompson seedless and saltana grapes direct from Upington on the Orange River on the Cape west coast to Britain.
Before, the grapes had to be trucked to Johannesburg by road before being airfreighted to Europe, Southwood said.
